description: Capabilities for Atlas's windows. Milestone 1's main window only needed core window chrome (minimize/maximize/close/resize). Milestone 2 adds the focus-companion window plus the permissions both windows need to create/show/hide/focus it from JS (see _lib/desktop/focus-companion-window.ts). Milestone 3 adds autostart:default for the Settings page's 'Launch Atlas when Windows starts' toggle (see _lib/desktop/autostart.ts) - the tray, global shortcut, and window-state persistence added in Milestone 3 are all native Rust (tray menu clicks, shortcut presses, window-state's own hooks), which the ACL system doesn't gate, so they need no capability entries here. Phase 19 adds allow-launch-application (autogenerated from src-tauri/permissions/autogenerated/launch_application.toml via build.rs's AppManifest - see os_launcher.rs) for the JARVIS 'open application' capability - the app's own commands are denied by default like everything else in Tauri 2's ACL, even ones defined in this same crate. Milestone 4 adds the widget-* window labels (see _lib/desktop/widgets/registry.ts and src-tauri/src/widgets.rs) - a new floating widget's real, running window is labeled 'widget-<id>' matching its registry entry, and needs its own entry here or JS window creation/show/hide fails silently against the ACL, exactly like focus-companion did in Milestone 2. Milestone 5 (Floating Widgets enable/show bug) adds `remote` - confirmed via live CDP testing against the real compiled app that EVERY permission in this file, even ones granted since Milestone 1/2, was being silently denied by the ACL ('not allowed by ACL'), because Atlas's windows all load an EXTERNAL URL (WebviewUrl::External, http://127.0.0.1:3000 - see lib.rs's own architecture note on why: Atlas is a real Next.js server, not a static bundle). Tauri's `local` capability flag (default true, and otherwise the only scope this file had) only covers content served from Tauri's OWN local asset protocol - it never applied to Atlas's actual windows, so NOTHING in this file ever actually took effect for real content, on ANY window, since Milestone 1. This was never caught earlier because nothing exercised a JS-invoked window IPC call through real interactive use of a compiled production build until the Settings 'Floating Widgets' toggle - the pre-existing Focus Companion JS show/hide path (used by 'TAKE QUEST') had the exact same latent bug, just never live-tested this way before.
